perspective:
From Angela Hwang’s perspective, she has access to:

- She and Kevin have been friends since high school. She knows he works in construction and has noticed he seems unhappy with his job.
- Angela invited Kevin to coffee. She heard Kevin say he was “alright” at first, then admit he is not happy, feels stuck and unfulfilled, and is just going through the motions.
- Kevin told her he has thought about changing jobs/careers but doesn’t know where to start and feels overwhelmed. Angela suggested they figure it out together; Kevin agreed and thanked her.
- Angela found job openings and a career counseling service, told Kevin about them, and encouraged him to check them out. Kevin thanked her and said he’d been thinking a lot and was interested in something creative, maybe design or architecture.
- Angela believed Kevin was hesitant, so she arranged a meeting with a career coach and told him. Kevin said she didn’t have to, appreciated it, but wasn’t sure he was ready. Angela encouraged him; Kevin agreed to give it a shot.
- Angela later checked in. Kevin told her the career coach was helpful, he had started online design courses, and he felt more confident. Angela offered more help; Kevin said just knowing she was there was enough and he’d ask if he needed anything.
- Angela believed Kevin had successfully transitioned to a new career, so she organized a small celebration party. Kevin thanked her, said he was grateful, and said he couldn’t have done it without her. They celebrated together.
- Angela’s own actions include inviting Kevin, expressing worry, suggesting options, sharing resources, arranging the career coach, checking in, offering support, expressing pride, and organizing the celebration.

She does not have access to Kevin’s unspoken private thoughts, details of his coaching sessions unless he told her, or any events she did not observe or hear about directly.
